risk: When the worker's write queue is full, SaveGuestWorldChanges runs a newer snapshot directly. A queued older worker closure could then run later and replace the newer file with stale content.
mitigation: Per destination path, a revision counter increments before worker Post/fallback selection.
Worker and fallback use the same closure and shared state. Commit lock serializes their check and staging/rename to prevent an old write after a new commit.
Stale callbacks do not touch disk; separate save slots have distinct state.
Common path-index lock is held only during registration; not during disk writes, preserving ordinary game-thread latency.
Inherited B06 atomic staged file replacement remains in force.
testing: actual production C++ guard and B06 file replace compiled in synthetic fixture; newest-before-old, multiple stale callbacks, two-slot separation and invalid destination are exercised
static assertions prove revision issued before Post and fallback uses same closure
inherits B06 staged file IO failure injection; B05 owner baseline, B04 reward owner, B03 reward retry, B02 lamp, B01 source contracts
known_limits: Pending last job may be lost on abrupt TerminateProcess/shutdown; the co-op worker is intentionally process-lifetime and does not flush on exit.
If the newest disk commit fails, the old on-disk world may remain, but this alone does not retry a new snapshot.
A full or switched-off worker queue can still force synchronous file IO as in B06; no new unbounded sleeps or background scan added.
No native Windows/NTFS test yet; production build #31 remains blocked.
No generalizable benchmark of BBHost versus BBPort and no real 5-player test.
Does not implement Supermedo's separate personal-world host-flag repair; GPL source ZIP release metadata was checked, archive bytes not inspected.
